about: When a device may write a synced copy on the account (Notes' marble/later, Reader's marble/reader and discover/seen), and when a write is done: reader.md §6, sync-guard.js. Write relays are the configured list (kind 10002), every one counted: one that failed to connect, answered CLOSED or never sent EOSE didn't answer. complete: more than half sent EOSE (reached). full: all of them did (only full reads count toward the escape). found: the newest copy's created_at the relays gave (0: none); seenAt: the newest this device has seen; misses: full reads in a row that missed it; expires: how long a copy lives (0: for good). written: more than half sent OK. retryAfter: the wait after the n-th failure in a row. writeList: your write relays from your relay list's tags, every one (no cap; .onion, LAN and ws:// count, as no answer when unreachable); none at all means the fast defaults. missesAgainst: misses are counted against one copy seen and start again when a newer one is seen.

cases.name: not reached (most write relays didn't answer): wait
never seen a copy, reached: write (merged with what's found)
found the copy seen, or newer: write
the copy seen is missing, every write relay answered: wait, the first miss
an older copy than seen, all answered: the second miss
the third full read in a row without it: start again from what your relays have
missing, but a write relay didn't answer (down, CLOSED, no EOSE): it may hold the copy, so no miss counts, never rebase
a seen list past its two weeks: gone, start again
a seen list within its two weeks, missing: wait

complete.name: one of three is down (failed to connect, so not asked): still reached, not full
one of three answered CLOSED (auth-required) or never sent EOSE: still reached, not full
the only write relay is down: not reached (a down relay still counts in the list)
no write relays known (the relay list wasn't found): not reached

written.name: one OK of three: pending, not done
OK from a relay not on the list doesn't count

writeList.name: every write relay counts, none capped: ten of them
read-only ones don't; unmarked and write ones do; once each, written alike
.onion, your own network and ws:// count too (a browser just never hears from them)
no write relays at all (every one read-only)

missesAgainst.name: counted against the copy seen now: kept
a newer copy seen since: starts again (else misses against an older copy rebase a newer one)
